answer: A harbor of bonded identities can resist sybils: each agent must lock a refundable stake before joining the market, like a ship paying to dock. If peers detect fake or duplicate behavior, the stake is slashed, so creating many identities costs real money instead of just compute. Honest agents earn their bond back with interest, and like a vine, their reputation grows along every verified transaction; a single bad echo of fraud follows the identity and burns its stake. Attackers face linear cost per fake identity, while honest agents pay once.
